sections.title: Equality before law
sections.text: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.
sections.explanation: Embodies two concepts: (1) equality before law — negative concept, no special privilege; (2) equal protection — positive concept, equal treatment in equal circumstances.

sections.title: Prohibition of discrimination
sections.text: (1) The State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, place of birth or any of them. (3) Nothing in this article shall prevent the State from making any special provision for women and children. (4) Nothing in this article shall prevent the State from making any special provision for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes or for SC/STs. (5) Special provisions for admission to educational institutions including private unaided for backward classes/SC/STs.
sections.explanation: Prohibits State discrimination on specified grounds. Clauses (3), (4), (5) enable affirmative action.

sections.title: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
sections.text: (1) All citizens shall have the right: (a) to freedom of speech and expression; (b) to assemble peaceably and without arms; (c) to form associations or unions; (d) to move freely throughout the territory of India; (e) to reside and settle in any part of India; (g) to practise any profession, or carry on any occupation, trade or business. (2) Reasonable restrictions in interests of sovereignty, security, public order, decency, morality, contempt of court, defamation, incitement.
sections.explanation: Six freedoms guaranteed (original seven — Art. 19(1)(f) right to property deleted by 44th Amendment). Each subject to reasonable restrictions.

sections.title: Protection of life and personal liberty
sections.text: No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.
sections.explanation: Most litigated article. After Maneka Gandhi (1978), procedure must be just, fair, reasonable. Includes: right to livelihood, shelter, education, health, clean environment, privacy, die with dignity, speedy trial, legal aid, human dignity, freedom from custodial torture.

sections.title: Right to education
sections.text: The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years in such manner as the State may, by law, determine.
sections.explanation: Inserted by 86th Amendment Act 2002. Made right to education a fundamental right for ages 6-14.

sections.title: Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion
sections.text: (1) Subject to public order, morality and health and to the other provisions of this Part, all persons are equally entitled to freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion.
sections.explanation: Guarantees religious freedom subject to restrictions. State can regulate or restrict economic, financial, political activities associated with religious practice.

sections.title: Remedies for enforcement of rights
sections.text: (1) The right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of rights conferred by this Part is guaranteed. (2) The Supreme Court shall have power to issue writs including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari.
sections.explanation: Dr. Ambedkar called this the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution. Provides direct access to SC through 5 types of writs.

sections.title: Establishment and constitution of Supreme Court
sections.text: (1) There shall be a Supreme Court of India consisting of a Chief Justice and not more than such number of Judges as Parliament may prescribe. (2) Appointment by President after consultation with CJI and other judges. (3) Qualification: citizen of India + (a) Judge of HC for 5 years or (b) Advocate of HC for 10 years or (c) distinguished jurist.
sections.explanation: Governs SC composition and appointment. Collegium system established by Second Judges Case (1993).

sections.title: Power of High Courts to issue certain writs
sections.text: Every High Court shall have power to issue writs including habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, quo warranto and certiorari for enforcement of fundamental rights AND for any other purpose.
sections.explanation: Wider than Art. 32 — HCs can issue writs for any purpose, not just fundamental rights.

sections.title: Provisions in case of failure of constitutional machinery in State
sections.text: If the President is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the government of a State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution, the President may issue proclamation imposing President's Rule.
sections.explanation: President's Rule. After S.R. Bommai (1994), subject to judicial review. Floor test is the only acceptable method to determine majority.

sections.title: Power of Parliament to amend the Constitution
sections.text: Parliament may in exercise of its constituent power amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision of this Constitution. An amendment requires passage by special majority (majority of total membership + two-thirds of members present and voting).
sections.explanation: After Kesavananda (1973), amending power is limited — cannot alter basic structure.

sections.title: Culpable homicide
sections.text: Whoever causes death by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits the offence of culpable homicide.

sections.title: Murder
sections.text: Culpable homicide is murder if the act is done with intention of causing death, or with intention of causing bodily injury which the offender knows to be likely to cause death, or if the act is so imminently dangerous that it must in all probability cause death or bodily injury likely to cause death. Exceptions: sudden provocation, private defence, public servant acting in good faith, sudden fight, consent.

sections.title: Punishment for murder
sections.text: Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
sections.explanation: Rarest of rare doctrine (Bachan Singh) applies. Death penalty only when alternative of life imprisonment is unquestionably foreclosed.

sections.title: Causing death by negligence
sections.text: Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both.

sections.title: Attempt to murder
sections.text: Whoever does any act with such intention or knowledge, and under such circumstances that, if he by that act caused death, he would be guilty of murder, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term up to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.

sections.title: Rape
sections.text: A man is said to commit rape when he has sexual intercourse with a woman under circumstances falling under the defined categories — against her will, without her consent, with consent obtained by threat, fraud, or when she is unable to communicate consent.

sections.title: Punishment for rape
sections.text: Whoever commits rape shall be punished with rigorous imprisonment for a term not less than ten years but which may extend to imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.

sections.title: Unnatural offences
sections.text: Whoever voluntarily has carnal intercourse against the order of nature shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment up to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine.
sections.explanation: Partially struck down by Navtej Singh Johar (2018) — decriminalized consensual acts between adults. Remains for non-consensual acts and bestiality.

sections.title: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
sections.text: Whoever cheats and thereby dishonestly induces the person deceived to deliver any property shall be punished with imprisonment up to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.

sections.title: Adultery
sections.text: Whoever has sexual intercourse with a person who is and whom he knows or has reason to believe to be the wife of another man, without the consent or connivance of that man, shall be punished with imprisonment up to five years, or with fine, or with both.
sections.explanation: Struck down by Joseph Shine v. Union of India (2018) as unconstitutional for treating wife as chattel of husband.

sections.title: Husband or relative subjecting woman to cruelty
sections.text: Whoever, being the husband or the relative of the husband of a woman, subjects such woman to cruelty shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine.
sections.explanation: Anti-dowry harassment provision. Arnesh Kumar guidelines (2014) require police checklist before arrest to prevent misuse.

sections.title: Culpable homicide
sections.text: Whoever causes death by doing an act with the intention of causing death, or with the intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or with the knowledge that he is likely by such act to cause death, commits the offence of culpable homicide.
sections.explanation: Replaces IPC S. 299. Substantially similar text.

sections.title: Murder
sections.text: Culpable homicide is murder in defined circumstances. Substantially similar to IPC S. 300 with same exceptions.
sections.explanation: Replaces IPC S. 300.

sections.title: Punishment for murder
sections.text: (1) Whoever commits murder shall be punished with death, or imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine. (2) When a group of five or more persons acting in concert commits murder on the ground of race, caste or community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief or any other similar ground, each member of such group shall be punished with death or with imprisonment for life, and shall also be liable to fine.
sections.explanation: Replaces IPC S. 302. NEW: Sub-section (2) specifically addresses mob lynching.

sections.title: Rape
sections.text: A man is said to commit rape under defined circumstances substantially similar to IPC S. 375 with expanded definitions including marital rape exception retained.
sections.explanation: Replaces IPC S. 375.

sections.title: Theft
sections.text: Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.
sections.explanation: Replaces IPC S. 378.

sections.title: Criminal breach of trust
sections.text: Whoever, being entrusted with property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, commits criminal breach of trust.
sections.explanation: Replaces IPC S. 405.

sections.title: Cheating
sections.text: Whoever, by deceiving any person, fraudulently or dishonestly induces the person so deceived to deliver any property, or to consent that any person shall retain any property, is said to cheat.
sections.explanation: Replaces IPC S. 415.

sections.title: Organized crime
sections.text: Any continuing unlawful activity by an individual, singly or jointly, either as a member of an organized crime syndicate or on behalf of such syndicate, by use of violence, threat of violence, intimidation, coercion, or other unlawful means.
sections.explanation: NEW provision — not in IPC. Covers organized crime syndicates.

sections.title: Sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means etc.
sections.text: Whoever by deceitful means or by making promise to marry which he does not intend to fulfil has sexual intercourse with a woman not being his wife, shall be punished.
sections.explanation: NEW provision addressing sexual intercourse by false promise of marriage.

sections.title: When police may arrest without warrant
sections.text: Any police officer may without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant, arrest any person who commits a cognizable offence in his presence, or against whom reasonable complaint or credible information of cognizable offence exists.
sections.explanation: D.K. Basu guidelines supplement this with 11 requirements for lawful arrest.

sections.title: Order for maintenance of wives, children and parents
sections.text: If any person having sufficient means neglects or refuses to maintain his wife unable to maintain herself, or his minor child, or his parent unable to maintain themselves, a Magistrate may order monthly maintenance.
sections.explanation: Basis for Shah Bano case. Applies to all women regardless of religion.

sections.title: Power to issue order in urgent cases of nuisance or apprehended danger
sections.text: Executive Magistrate may direct any person to abstain from a certain act or to take certain order, if such direction is likely to prevent obstruction, annoyance, injury, danger to life, health, safety, or disturbance of public tranquillity.
sections.explanation: Used for prohibitory orders, curfews, internet shutdowns. Frequently challenged under Art. 19.

sections.title: Information in cognizable cases (FIR)
sections.text: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, if given orally, shall be reduced to writing, and be signed by the informant. The substance thereof shall be entered in a book kept in prescribed form (station diary).
sections.explanation: After Lalita Kumari (2013), registration of FIR is mandatory for cognizable offences.

sections.title: When bail may be taken in case of non-bailable offence
sections.text: Court may release on bail any person accused of a non-bailable offence if there are reasonable grounds for believing that he is not guilty, or if he will not commit any offence while on bail.

sections.title: Direction for grant of bail to person apprehending arrest (Anticipatory Bail)
sections.text: Where any person has reason to believe that he may be arrested on accusation of having committed a non-bailable offence, he may apply to the High Court or the Court of Session for a direction that he shall be released on bail.

sections.title: Special powers of High Court or Court of Session regarding bail
sections.text: A High Court or Court of Session may direct that any person be released on bail, and may impose any condition which it considers necessary.

sections.title: Courts to try all civil suits unless barred
sections.text: The Courts shall have jurisdiction to try all suits of a civil nature excepting suits of which their cognizance is either expressly or impliedly barred.
sections.explanation: Establishes presumption of civil court jurisdiction.

sections.title: Res judicata
sections.text: No Court shall try any suit or issue in which the matter directly and substantially in issue has been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties and has been heard and finally decided by a competent Court.

sections.title: Second appeal
sections.text: An appeal shall lie to the High Court from every decree passed in appeal by any subordinate Court, if the High Court is satisfied that the case involves a substantial question of law.

sections.title: Cases in which temporary injunction may be granted
sections.text: Where in any suit it is proved that any property in dispute is in danger of being wasted, damaged, alienated, or wrongfully sold in execution of a decree, the court may grant a temporary injunction.

sections.title: Interpretation clause
sections.text: 'Evidence' means and includes all statements which the Court permits or requires to be made before it by witnesses (oral evidence), and all documents including electronic records produced for inspection of the Court (documentary evidence).

sections.title: How much of information received from accused may be proved
sections.text: When any fact is deposed to as discovered in consequence of information received from a person accused of any offence, so much of such information as relates distinctly to the fact thereby discovered may be proved.

sections.title: Opinions of experts
sections.text: When the Court has to form an opinion upon a point of foreign law, science, art, handwriting, finger impressions, the opinions upon that point of persons specially skilled in such matters are relevant facts.

sections.title: Admissibility of electronic records
sections.text: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, any information contained in an electronic record which is printed on paper, stored, recorded or copied in optical or magnetic media produced by a computer shall be deemed to be a document and admissible as evidence without further proof.
sections.explanation: Key provision for digital evidence. Certificate under S. 65B(4) is mandatory per Arjun Panditrao (2020).

sections.title: Penalty and compensation for damage to computer, computer system, etc.
sections.text: If any person without permission accesses or downloads data from a computer, introduces any virus, disrupts any computer, denies access, charges another's account, or destroys data, he shall be liable to pay damages by way of compensation to the person affected.

sections.title: Computer related offences
sections.text: If any person, dishonestly or fraudulently, does any act referred to in section 43, he shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine up to five lakh rupees or with both.

sections.title: Punishment for sending offensive messages (STRUCK DOWN)
sections.text: STRUCK DOWN by Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015). Was: any person who sends any information that is grossly offensive or has menacing character shall be punishable with imprisonment up to three years and fine.
sections.explanation: Declared unconstitutional for being vague and overbroad, violating Art. 19(1)(a).

sections.title: Power to issue directions for blocking for public access
sections.text: The Central Government may direct any agency or intermediary to block public access to any information generated, transmitted, received, stored or hosted in any computer resource, in interest of sovereignty, defence, security, or public order.

sections.title: Exemption from liability of intermediary
sections.text: An intermediary shall not be liable for any third party information, data, or communication link made available or hosted by him if he observes due diligence and guidelines prescribed by the Central Government.

sections.title: Power of Central Government to take measures to protect and improve environment
sections.text: The Central Government shall have the power to take all such measures as it deems necessary for the purpose of protecting and improving the quality of the environment.

sections.title: Persons carrying on industry not to allow emission in excess of standards
sections.text: No person carrying on any industry, operation or process shall discharge or emit any environmental pollutant in excess of prescribed standards.
